name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q01 - Serial repetition of organs in animal body

questiontext.text: In some animal groups, the body is found divided into compartments with serial repetition of at least some organs. This characteristic feature is called

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In animal body plans, structural division of the body into repeating units can take different forms, each defined by specific anatomical and developmental criteria.

Step 2: Evaluation
Metamerism is the phenomenon in which the body is externally and internally divided into segments (metameres) with a serial repetition of at least some organs, as seen in annelids such as earthworms. By contrast, general segmentation does not necessarily involve internal compartmentalisation with serial organ repetition, metagenesis refers to alternation of generations between polyp and medusa forms in cnidarians, and metamorphosis refers to post-embryonic transformation from larva to adult.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The characteristic feature of body division into compartments with serial repetition of at least some organs is called metamerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q02 - Cells that differentiate to perform different functions

questiontext.text: Given below are types of cells present in some animals. Which of the following cells can differentiate to perform different functions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Certain undifferentiated reserve cells in lower invertebrates retain developmental plasticity and can transform into specialized cell types as required for growth, repair, or regeneration.

Step 2: Evaluation
Interstitial cells (found in cnidarians such as Hydra) are totipotent cells capable of differentiating into various specialized cells, including nematocytes, germ cells, and nerve cells. In contrast, choanocytes (collar cells in sponges for water circulation and feeding), gastrodermal cells (lining the gastrovascular cavity for digestion), and nematocytes (stinging cells in cnidarians for defense and prey capture) are already terminally differentiated cells with specific roles.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The cells that can differentiate to perform different functions are interstitial cells.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q03 - Animals sharing a four chambered heart

questiontext.text: Which one of the following sets of animals share a four chambered heart?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vertebrate heart structure varies across classes: amphibians have a three-chambered heart, most reptiles have an incompletely divided three-chambered heart, whereas birds and mammals possess a completely divided four-chambered heart.

Step 2: Evaluation
Among reptiles, crocodiles are an exception because they possess a completely four-chambered heart with two auricles and two ventricles. Birds (Aves) and mammals (Mammalia) also have four-chambered hearts. Lizards, turtles, and amphibians have three-chambered hearts.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The set of animals that all share a four-chambered heart is crocodiles, birds, and mammals.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q04 - Pair of animals with non glandular skin

questiontext.text: Which of the following pairs of animals has non glandular skin

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Integumentary glands differ across vertebrate classes. Reptiles are adapted to terrestrial life with dry, cornified skin covered by epidermal scales or scutes, lacking skin glands.

Step 2: Evaluation
Chameleon and turtle both belong to Class Reptilia and possess dry, non-glandular skin. In contrast, frogs (Amphibia) have moist, glandular skin; pigeons (Aves) have an oil (uropygial) gland at the base of the tail; and tigers (Mammalia) have sweat and sebaceous glands in their skin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The pair of animals with non-glandular skin is chameleon and turtle.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q05 - Common characteristic of birds and mammals

questiontext.text: Birds and mammals share one of the following characteristics as a common feature.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Birds (Class Aves) and mammals (Class Mammalia) are both endothermic vertebrates capable of regulating and maintaining a constant internal body temperature independently of external environmental fluctuations.

Step 2: Evaluation
Being warm-blooded (homoiothermous) is a shared characteristic of both birds and mammals. Pneumatic (hollow, air-filled) bones are characteristic of birds, viviparity is characteristic of most mammals (whereas birds are oviparous), and pigmented skin is not a universal distinguishing feature shared exclusively across both classes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The common feature shared by birds and mammals is that both are warm blooded.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q06 - Animals belonging to a single taxonomic group

questiontext.text: Which one of the following sets of animals belong to a single taxonomic group?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Common names of animals can be misleading and do not always reflect their true taxonomic classification; animals in a single taxonomic group share common evolutionary ancestry and diagnostic anatomical features.

Step 2: Evaluation
Monkey, chimpanzee, and man all belong to Class Mammalia (and Order Primates). In the other sets, cuttlefish (Mollusca), jellyfish (Cnidaria), silverfish (Arthropoda), dogfish (Chondrichthyes), and starfish (Echinodermata) belong to different phyla; bat (Mammalia), pigeon (Aves), and butterfly (Arthropoda) belong to different classes/phyla; and silkworm (Arthropoda), tapeworm (Platyhelminthes), and earthworm (Annelida) belong to different phyla.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The set of animals belonging to a single taxonomic group is monkey, chimpanzee, and man.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q07 - Identifying incorrect statement on animal body plans

questiontext.text: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animal phyla are classified based on germ layers, symmetry, and nature of the body cavity (coelom). Platyhelminthes are triploblastic and acoelomate, whereas Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomate.

Step 2: Evaluation
Fasciola (liver fluke) belongs to Phylum Platyhelminthes, which are acoelomates (lacking a body cavity), not pseudocoelomates. The other statements are biologically accurate: Obelia (Cnidaria) is diploblastic with an undifferentiated mesoglea layer between ectoderm and endoderm; adult Asterias (Echinodermata) exhibits radial symmetry; and Taenia (Platyhelminthes) is triploblastic.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statement is that Fasciola is a pseudocoelomate animal.

answer.text: Mesoglea is present in between ectoderm and endoderm in Obelia.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q08 - Identifying incorrect statement on invertebrate physiology

questiontext.text: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Within Phylum Arthropoda, different classes use specialized excretory organs suited to their habitat and physiology—insects use Malpighian tubules, whereas crustaceans use antennal (green) glands.

Step 2: Evaluation
While cockroaches (Class Insecta) excrete waste through Malpighian tubules, prawns (Class Crustacea) excrete waste through green glands (antennal glands), not Malpighian tubules. The remaining statements are true: ctenophores use eight external rows of ciliated comb plates for locomotion, Fasciola uses flame cells for osmoregulation and excretion, and earthworms are hermaphrodites that undergo cross-fertilisation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statement is that in cockroaches and prawns excretion of waste material occurs through malpighian tubules.

answer.text: In cockroaches and prawns excretion of waste material occurs through malpighian tubules.
In ctenophores, locomotion is mediated by comb plates.
Earthworms are hermaphrodites and yet cross fertilization take place among them.

questiontext.text: Which one of the following is oviparous?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Most mammals are viviparous (giving birth to live young), with a notable exception in egg-laying mammals (monotremes), which are oviparous.

Step 2: Evaluation
Platypus (Ornithorhynchus) is an egg-laying (oviparous) mammal. Flying fox (bat), elephant, and whale are all viviparous placental mammals that give birth to live young.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The oviparous animal among the given mammals is platypus.

questiontext.text: Which one of the following is a non-poisonous snake?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Snakes (reptiles) are classified into poisonous (venomous) species, which possess poison glands and fangs, and non-poisonous species, which kill prey by constriction or swallowing.

Step 2: Evaluation
Python is a large non-poisonous constrictor snake. Cobra (Naja), viper (Vipera), and krait (Bungarus) are all well-known poisonous snakes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The non-poisonous snake is python.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MATCHINGMCQ_Q11 - Matching animals with levels of organisation

questiontext.text:
Match the following list of animals with their level of organisation.

Division of Labour (Column I) Animal (Column II)
A. Organ level i. Pheretima
B. Cellular aggregate level ii. Fasciola
C. Tissue level iii. Spongilla
D. Organ system level iv. Obelia

Choose the correct match showing division of labour with animal example.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Multicellular animals exhibit progressive levels of structural organisation: cellular aggregate level in Porifera, tissue level in Coelenterata, organ level in Platyhelminthes, and organ system level from Aschelminthes onwards (including Annelida).

Step 2: Evaluation
Fasciola belongs to Phylum Platyhelminthes and exhibits the organ level of organisation. Spongilla belongs to Phylum Porifera and shows the cellular aggregate level. Obelia belongs to Phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria) and displays the tissue level. Pheretima (earthworm) belongs to Phylum Annelida and possesses the organ system level of organisation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: Organ level with Fasciola, Cellular aggregate level with Spongilla, Tissue level with Obelia, and Organ system level with Pheretima.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MCQ_Q12 - Body cavity not lined by mesoderm

questiontext.text: Body cavity is the cavity present between body wall and gut wall. In some animals the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm. Such animals are called

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The presence or absence of a cavity between the body wall and the gut wall, and whether it is lined by mesoderm, is a fundamental criterion for animal classification.

Step 2: Evaluation
When the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm and instead the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm, the cavity is called a pseudocoelom and the animals are called pseudocoelomates (e.g., Aschelminthes). Animals lacking a body cavity are acoelomates, animals with a mesoderm-lined body cavity are coelomates, and haemocoelomates have a blood-filled cavity (haemocoel).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Animals in which the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm are called pseudocoelomates.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMALKINGDOM_MATCHINGMCQ_Q13 - Matching animal phyla with characteristic features

questiontext.text:
Match the column A with column B and choose the correct option

Column I Column II
A. Porifera i. Canal system
B. Aschelminthes ii. Water-vascular system
C. Annelida iii. Muscular pharynx
D. Arthropoda iv. Jointed appendages
E. Echinodermata v. Metameres

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each major invertebrate phylum possesses distinctive anatomical features that aid in identification and classification.

Step 2: Evaluation
Porifera is characterized by a water transport or canal system. Aschelminthes have an alimentary canal that is complete with a well-developed muscular pharynx. Annelida exhibits metameric segmentation with body rings called metameres. Arthropoda is named for its jointed appendages. Echinodermata is uniquely characterized by a water-vascular system used for locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: Porifera with canal system, Aschelminthes with muscular pharynx, Annelida with metameres, Arthropoda with jointed appendages, and Echinodermata with water-vascular system.
